title: The cable from Lee Bouveau and AGVA's call for a bond
summary: He got a letter and cable from an agent, learned he was a black man named Lee Bouveau, and AGVA advised a bond.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So what I did, I got a letter from England from a fellow who was in Germany concerning this review that I had and if I had

and if I had this over in Germany I could make some money and also I could get in a picture there with it. And then he found out the picture, he told me I would have $1,000 a week all expenses paid, round-trip transportation. Okay? That's good, it will only take me a week, I'll make this, you know. Don't forget now, Buck has to be off -- he's out, but he was going through the same routine that he went before he got in. And this is what I didn't want.

So I went over there and did this gig where I couldn't come on back. But that's when I got stuck. I got over there and this guy was a negro. And I didn't know it, I wouldn't have went. (Inaudible) was telling me to get a bond put up before I go, a man who was a manager for so many years and had been nil for 12 years and I'd been asking for the Ziegfeld Follies for 12 years and met him the same way. So, he wanted to manage me. And he got me a job for Hollywood, brought back the song I'm going to do, the Gettysburg -- the speech of

Gettysburg I was going to do in the song. I was supposed to learn this song. When I got the message from Germany about coming over to do this number. And I talked to him about it. He says, if you want to go -- I says, yeh. So they sent a cable -- the cable with the ticket, plus asked the airline to encourage me to come. It was a reliable firm. This was the agent that sent me the telegram and all.

I couldn't think that was colored. Lee Bouveau? However, I showed this to this man that was going to manage me -- forgot his name now -- anyway I showed it to him and I tell A.G.V.A. about it. They still think I should have a bond put up.
I thought they couldn't want to put up a little bond -- I said it would be all right.
